bull.b: Revenue increased 13.1% in 2025 and 20.9% in 2024, indicating sustained demand and market traction across multiple periods. Continued top-line expansion can support scale benefits, investment in product development, and broader customer reach if growth converts into healthier margins.

The company remains conservatively financed, with very low debt relative to equity. This reduces balance-sheet pressure, preserves borrowing capacity, and provides greater flexibility to fund operations or strategic investment while limiting the financial risk associated with interest obligations.

Strong positive cash flow in 2023 and 2024, including cash generation broadly aligned with 2024 earnings, demonstrates that the business has previously converted performance into internal funding. That capability could support investment and resilience if cash generation normalizes.

bear.t: Negative Operating and Free Cash Flow
bear.b: The 2025 swing to negative operating and free cash flow weakens earnings quality and reduces internally generated funding. If this volatility persists, the company may have less flexibility to invest in growth, absorb setbacks, or support operations without relying on its balance-sheet resources.

Profitability deteriorated sharply despite continued revenue growth, with net margin falling to about 2.4% and operating profit near breakeven. This raises concerns about earnings durability because top-line expansion is currently producing materially less profit and may not translate into dependable returns.

The delayed release of second-quarter results, combined with warnings of significant operating and net losses, signals heightened operational and financial uncertainty. Extended reporting disruption can consume management attention, complicate oversight, and make near-term business performance less predictable.
